title: Pro-etale closed-support triangle before constructible restriction
statement:
Let $T$ be Noetherian, let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a
closed immersion, and
let $j$ be its open complement. For a finite ring $A$, let
$Ri^!$ denote the right adjoint of the
direct image $i_*$ on the
pro-etale sites, taken on
the ambient ordinary derived categories, and let $Rj_*$ and $j^*$
be the direct image and the
inverse image of the open immersion $j$. In addition to the
open–closed triangle,
one has

$$
i_*Ri^!K\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K
\longrightarrow i_*Ri^!K[1]
\qquad(K\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)).
$$

No constructibility of $Ri^!K$ is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Work on the small skeletons and in the common sheaf universe of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For the finite ring $A$, use the sheaf of rings $A_S$ and left module sheaves of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], for $S=T,U,Z$; no commutativity of $A$ is needed. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] these abelian categories are Grothendieck. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to a complex representing $K$ to choose a quasi-isomorphism $K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective and every $I^q$ injective. Use the exact inverse images with transported coefficient actions of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Define an additive sheaf functor $H$ on left $A_T$-modules by $H(N)=i^*\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$, using the open adjunction unit, and on morphisms by the induced kernel map followed by $i^*$. Kernels here are the sectionwise kernels of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Applying $H$ termwise preserves shifts and mapping-cone matrices, so its composite with derived localization is exact on homotopy categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], its total right derived functor $RH$ exists and $RH(K)$ is represented by $H(I)$. Step 7 proves that $RH$ is the right adjoint $Ri^!$ in the statement and identifies its counit. No adjunction for $H$ has been assumed here.

source.place: ## Proof, choosing a K-injective resolution with injective terms and computing the closed right adjoint

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-proetale-open-derived-image] to the resolution $I$ of Step 1. It identifies $j^*$ with exact restriction, including coefficients and units, and makes $j^*I$ K-injective. Thus $Rj_*j^*K$ is represented by $j_*j^*I$, and the derived open unit is represented by the termwise restriction $I\to j_*j^*I$.

source.place: Proof: exact open restriction, K-injectivity, and computation of the derived open unit

proof.text: For an object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $V_U=V\times_TU$ and let $a:V_U\to V$ be the open inclusion. It is a monomorphism by clause (4) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], again using auxiliary ring $\mathbf Z$ for the geometric assertion. Let $P_V=A_T[h_V]$ be the free module presheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] and $L_V=P_V^\#$ its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The map $P_{V_U}\to P_V$ sends $e_b$ to $e_{ab}$ at an object $W$. It commutes with restriction because both composites send $r e_b$ to $r|_c e_{abc}$. Since $a$ is monic, the basis map $\operatorname{Hom}(W,V_U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$ is injective. A free-module element in its kernel has every coefficient zero, so the presheaf map is componentwise injective, hence monic. Exact module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] gives a monomorphism $L_{V_U}\to L_V$.

source.place: ## Proof, the monomorphism of free module sheaves for the open part

proof.text: The free-presheaf bijection [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] and the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] give $\operatorname{Hom}(L_V,N)=N(V)$. Precomposing with $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ corresponds to restriction: the map associated to $x\in N(V)$ sends $e_b$ to $x|_b$, so on the identity generator of $V_U$ its precomposition has value $x|_a$. For $y\in I^q(V_U)$ extend the corresponding $L_{V_U}\to I^q$ across the monomorphism of Step 3, using injectivity in the precise sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The extension corresponds to $x\in I^q(V)$ with $x|_a=y$. Hence $I^q\to j_*j^*I^q$ is sectionwise surjective for every site object $V$. It is epic: two sheaf maps out of its target agreeing after it agree on every section by such lifts, and hence are equal by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: ## Proof, injectivity extends sections and proves the termwise surjectivity

proof.text: The complement $j$ is quasi-compact. For an open cover of any open subset $O\subseteq T$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] to the nonempty family of complements in $T$ of finite unions of cover members. A minimal complement gives a maximal finite union; adjoining any cover member cannot enlarge it, so it equals $O$. Hence every open of $T$ is quasi-compact, including $U\cap V$ for every affine open $V\subseteq T$. This is the quasi-compactness condition for $j$.

source.place: Proof: Noetherianity supplies the quasi-compact-complement hypothesis

proof.text: Set $F^q=\ker(I^q\to j_*j^*I^q)$. By Step 2 the unit restricts to the identity over $U$, so $j^*F^q=0$. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] with the commutative coefficient sheaves for $B=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, where $n$ is the additive order of $1_A$; their canonical inverse-image identifications are supplied by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Step 5 supplies quasi-compactness. These verify the commutative essential-image hypothesis of [lem-exc-proetale-supported-kernel-complex]. That lemma transfers supported units to the given $A$-modules and gives $j^*i_*M=0$. Since Step 4 makes each open unit epic, its complex clause identifies $F\cong i_*H(I)$ and gives $0\to i_*H(I)\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$, naturally, with the kernel-inclusion first arrow.

source.place: Proof: supported kernel identification and assembly of the short exact complex sequence

proof.text: Step 5 shows that every open subset of $T$ is quasi-compact; in particular intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact, so $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $j$ is quasi-compact. Apply clause (2) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] with $X=T$ and $B=A_T$; that statement allows a noncommutative ring sheaf. Its closed coefficient ring is $i^{-1}A_T$. Restriction of scalars along the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_i:i^{-1}A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_Z$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] is an isomorphism of the module categories. Under it the transported inverse image $i^*$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] is the clause's $i^*$, both being $i^{-1}$ on underlying sheaves. The direct images agree too: on $(i_*G)(W)=G(Z\times_TW)$ both act through $A_T\to i_*i^{-1}A_T\xrightarrow{i_*c_i}i_*A_Z$, which is the map $\rho$ adjoint to $c_i$. Hence $i_*$ is exact and fully faithful on left $A_Z$-module sheaves, for every finite ring $A$. The supported-unit and vanishing assertions from Step 6 and the restriction identification from Step 2 verify the remaining hypotheses of [lem-exc-proetale-derived-adjunction-triangle]. It identifies $H$ as the sheaf right adjoint, $RH$ as the right adjoint $Ri^!$ on the unbounded derived categories, and $i_*H(I)\to I$ as its derived counit after localization. In particular $i_*H(I)$ represents $i_*Ri^!K$.

source.place: Proof: identification of the exceptional right adjoint and its counit

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the short exact sequence of Step 6. Its vertices represent $i_*Ri^!K$, $K$, and $Rj_*j^*K$ by Steps 1, 2, and 7. Its first two arrows are the closed counit and open unit by Steps 7 and 2. Thus it yields exactly $i_*Ri^!K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to i_*Ri^!K[1]$. No constructibility or boundedness of $K$ or $Ri^!K$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-12f097c2e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item statement, which matches the master and main-20261015 sources word for word and keeps its Lean record (noncommutative finite A in scope); all 8 steps; the three new statement-only nodes; and the statement of every cited node. The route is the unit sk-prop-sf-localization; no SGA source is cited. Steps 1-6 and 8 check out: the K-injective resolution has injective terms, the open-restriction mono comes from clause (4) of weakly-etale-localization, the injective lifting makes the termwise units epic, Noetherian implies every open is quasi-compact, the supported kernels are transferred through B=Z/n, and the ses-triangle gives the counit and unit maps. One fault, which I repaired (E1/C4): Step 7 cited lem-exc-proetale-closed-exact and lem-exc-proetale-closed-fully-faithful for an arbitrary finite ring A. Both are stated only for commutative coefficients (the convention of def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations), so they do not cover A=M_2(F_2). The corrected Step 7 cites clause (2) of det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf instead. That node is on the route (unit sk-prop-sf-closed-unit), passed review on 2026-10-17, and holds for any ring sheaf B on a qcqs X with quasi-compact j. It is applied with B=A_T: T is qcqs and j is quasi-compact by Step 5, and the coefficients are transported along c_i from prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, which matches i^* and i_* (action through rho). I recomputed proof_deps, and the dependency closure has no cycle. All three new nodes are true, none is circular and none restates a clause of the item. I tested them on A=0, A=M_2(F_2), U empty and Z empty. Duplicate candidates checked and rejected: open-unit, kinjective-restrict-localized, closed-support (commutative only) and det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction (condensed coefficients). The first two clauses of supported-kernel-complex also follow from det-sf, but its complex clause is stated nowhere else, so I kept it. lean.statement: theorem exists_proEtale_closedSupportTriangle {T Z U : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian T] [CompactSpace T] (i : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hU : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ) (A : Type (u + 1)) [Ring A] [Finite A] [TopologicalSpace A] [DiscreteTopology A] : ∃ (iPush : FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory Z A ⥤ FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory T A) (jPull : FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory T A ⥤ FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory U A), Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u + 1} (F := Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange i) (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (K := Scheme.ProEt.topology Z) (finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap i A)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ iPush) ∧ Nonempty ((finiteCoefficientModulePullback j A).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ≅ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ jPull) ∧ ∃ (iShriek : FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory T A ⥤ FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory Z A) (jPush : FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory U A ⥤ FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory T A) (closedAdj : iPush ⊣ iShriek) (openAdj : jPull ⊣ jPush), ∀ K : FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory T A, ∃ δ : jPush.obj (jPull.obj K) ⟶ (iPush.obj (iShriek.obj K))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧, Triangle.mk (closedAdj.counit.app K) (openAdj.unit.app K) δ ∈ distTriang (FiniteCoefficientDerivedCategory T A)
lean.note: The ambient i_* and j^* are characterized by localization of their actual module functors; the right adjoints then specify Ri^! and Rj_* uniquely up to canonical adjunction isomorphism. This avoids the commutativity restriction on the older chosen derived-direct-image API. No mathematical hypothesis, coefficient category or derived category is changed.
